newsitem.title: USA: Chiron unit's Vitrasert cleared in EU.
newsitem.headline: Chiron unit's Vitrasert cleared in EU.

text.p: Chiron Corp's Chiron Vision said on Tuesday the European Commission granted marketing authorization for its Vitrasert implant, for drug delivery to the eye, in 15 countries of the European Union.
Vitrasert is a drug delivery system to provide local, sustained therapy of the eye for the treatment of cytomegalovirus retinitis in people with AIDS, Chiron said.
Europe's Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products had recommended approval for Vitrasert on behalf of the European Agency for the Evaluation of Medicinal Products, it said.
Vitrasert Implant releases the antiviral agent ganciclovir directly to the disease site, the company said.
In November, 1996, the European Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products recommended Vitrasert as a first-line therapy against such retinitis, Chiron said.
The company said cytomegalovirus retinitis affected an estimated 30,000 to 60,000 people annually worldwide.

Data from Chiron Vision's Phase III trial of 188 AIDS patients with newly diagnosed cytomegalovirus retinitis demonstrated that time to disease progression was significantly delayed for patients who received the Vitrasert therapy, the company said.
